# Tan Lines

> The unvarnished history of Melanotan II. A publication at melanotanii.com.
> The Record is the dated file: timeline, regulatory watch, and articles.

Tan Lines does not sell, source, or provide usage guidance for Melanotan II or any unapproved compound. Nothing here is medical advice. Melanotan II is not approved by any regulator for any use.

## The Record

- [Timeline](https://melanotanii.com/timeline/): one origin, three strands, forty years
- [Regulatory watch](https://melanotanii.com/regulatory/): living scoreboard for MT-II and melanocortin photoprotection — legal status by country, dated
- [All articles](https://melanotanii.com/articles/): history, science, demand, cautionary tale, next agonist

## Articles

- [Melanotan II pharmacokinetics: why one dose does everything](https://melanotanii.com/articles/a-drug-with-no-address/): Why one dose of Melanotan II tans, sickens, and arouses at once: its pharmacokinetics give it no address. It floods the body and outlasts the signal it mimics.
- [The Barbie drug: how Melanotan II built a gray market](https://melanotanii.com/articles/barbie-drug-gray-market/): Never approved anywhere, Melanotan II sold anyway — through forums, gyms, and 'research chemical' sites. How the gray market formed, and what it costs.
- [How the tan became desirable: Chanel, the Riviera, the sunbed](https://melanotanii.com/articles/how-a-suntan-became-desirable/): For most of history a tan meant labor; then, in one decade, it flipped. How Chanel, the Riviera, and the sunbed made tanned skin aspirational.
- [Does a tan protect your skin? How eumelanin blocks UV](https://melanotanii.com/articles/how-a-tan-protects-skin/): A tan is the body's sunscreen: eumelanin absorbing UV before it reaches DNA. How melanin protects skin — and why that was Melanotan's target.
- [How Melanotan II is sold now: the DTC supply stack](https://melanotanii.com/articles/how-its-sold-now/): Research-chemical storefronts, banned hashtags, influencer commissions, salon shelves, disguised payments — the supply machine that sells Melanotan II now.
- [How Melanotan II escaped the lab: patents and the gray market](https://melanotanii.com/articles/how-the-science-escaped-the-lab/): Melanotan II's recipe was published in journals and patents, then orphaned by its developers. Public structure plus real demand made the gray market inevitable.
- [MC1R variants: why not everyone can tan the same way](https://melanotanii.com/articles/mc1r-variants-not-universal/): Red hair is the loud end. Most MC1R variants are quieter: r alleles, heterozygotes, East Asian R163Q. A future agonist would not reach everyone who burns.
- [Melanotan I vs Melanotan II: two peptides, two fates](https://melanotanii.com/articles/melanotan-1-vs-melanotan-2/): Melanotan I vs Melanotan II: near-identical peptides from the same Arizona lab. One became an approved medicine; the other, the gray market's favorite. Why.
- [Scenesse (afamelanotide): the approved sun drug you can't get](https://melanotanii.com/articles/middle-ground-agonist-already-exists/): Afamelanotide (Scenesse) is an approved melanocortin drug that protects skin from light — locked in a rare-disease label. Why, and what a breakout would take.
- [Melanotan vs melatonin: one letter, completely different](https://melanotanii.com/articles/not-melatonin/): Melanotan and melatonin are one letter apart and nothing else alike: a sleep supplement versus an unapproved tanning peptide. Why the mix-up matters.
- [Melanocortin receptors: why Melanotan II does more than tan](https://melanotanii.com/articles/one-hormone-five-receptors/): Why Melanotan II tans, suppresses appetite, and affects libido at once: one non-selective agonist hitting all five melanocortin receptors.
- [Tanorexia and the opioid your skin makes in the sun](https://melanotanii.com/articles/tanorexia-the-opioid-your-skin-makes/): UV light makes skin manufacture its own opioid — the hidden reward inside every tan. The science of tanning dependence, and what it says about Melanotan.
- [The Melanotan II self-experiment that found a libido drug](https://melanotanii.com/articles/the-accident-inside-melanotan/): A University of Arizona self-experiment with Melanotan II produced an eight-hour erection — and pointed the way to an FDA-approved libido drug.
- [How a photoprotective melanocortin drug could reach everyone](https://melanotanii.com/articles/the-beachhead-indications/): How a photoprotective melanocortin drug could reach everyone: beachhead indications, from approved EPP to a vitiligo trial now in Phase III.
- [Melanotan nasal sprays on TikTok: the influencer era](https://melanotanii.com/articles/the-influencer-era/): How Melanotan II went viral: nasal sprays, flavored drops, and the TikTok 'vacation peptide' re-packaged an unregulated injectable for the open market.
- [Melanotan II and moles: what dermatologists actually fear](https://melanotanii.com/articles/the-mole-problem/): Melanotan II darkens and multiplies moles — and the deeper danger is diagnostic: the case reports, the melanoma question, and the signals you lose.
- [Oral Melanotan II capsules and gummies: why they can't work](https://melanotanii.com/articles/the-pill-that-wasnt/): Melanotan II sold as a capsule, gummy, or drink can't work: a cyclic peptide doesn't survive digestion. What 'oral melanotan' actually is.
- [Why 'prevents skin cancer' is the hardest claim to prove](https://melanotanii.com/articles/the-prevention-trial-problem/): Proving a drug prevents skin cancer needs one of the longest, largest trials in medicine. Why the evidence bar — not the chemistry — is the real wall.
- [Melanotan II side effects: what the evidence actually says](https://melanotanii.com/articles/the-side-effect-ledger/): Melanotan II side effects, sorted by evidence: the documented acute and pigment effects, and the rare serious events that reach the medical literature.
- [The tan without the sun: how Melanotan skips the UV damage](https://melanotanii.com/articles/the-tan-without-the-sun/): A suntan is a wound response: pigment made only after UV has damaged skin DNA. Melanotan's idea was the protection without the damage.
- [Is Melanotan II legal in the U.S.? Three regulatory doors](https://melanotanii.com/articles/the-three-doors/): Is Melanotan II legal in the U.S.? It's unapproved — but the technology isn't. The three doors: FDA approval, compounding, and the gray market.
- [Melanotan II and longevity: the wellness-menu rebrand](https://melanotanii.com/articles/the-wellness-menu/): Wellness clinics now sell Melanotan II as a longevity peptide. Real melanocortin drugs exist — approved, selective, monitored. This isn't one of them.
- [What a safe tanning drug would actually have to be](https://melanotanii.com/articles/what-a-safe-tanning-drug-requires/): The four requirements a general-public photoprotective drug must clear — and how far today's science already is toward each. Analysis, labeled as such.
- [Melanotan II enforcement: what the warnings actually did](https://melanotanii.com/articles/what-the-warnings-actually-did/): Regulators seized sites, parcels, and sellers. Australia made possession a crime. The market moved to nasal sprays. Why enforcement keeps losing.
- [Gray-market Melanotan II: you can't know what's in the vial](https://melanotanii.com/articles/whats-in-the-vial/): Gray-market Melanotan II comes from unknown labs: purity, sterility, and dose are all assumptions — and assumptions have sent people to the ER.
- [Where Melanotan came from: the Arizona sunscreen quest](https://melanotanii.com/articles/where-melanotan-came-from/): Melanotan II began as 1980s melanoma-prevention research at the University of Arizona — an injectable sunscreen. The origin story of the tanning peptide.
- [Who owned Melanotan: the patent trail to Clinuvel and Palatin](https://melanotanii.com/articles/who-owned-melanotan/): How a University of Arizona peptide became two FDA drugs and a gray-market staple: the patent trail from Hruby and Hadley to Clinuvel and Palatin.
- [Who would pay for a sun-drug trial: the sponsor problem](https://melanotanii.com/articles/who-would-pay-for-the-trial/): Clinuvel profits from a rare-disease implant. Novo funds prevention trials insurers pay for. A general-public sun drug needs both, and has neither.
- [Why Melanotan II went underground: a want, not a need](https://melanotanii.com/articles/why-a-cosmetic-went-underground/): Why Melanotan II became the most self-injected unapproved drug: it served a want, not a need — and wants don't wait for clinical trials.
- [Why redheads burn: the MC1R gene and the pigment switch](https://melanotanii.com/articles/why-redheads-burn-mc1r/): Red hair, freckles, and burning instead of tanning trace to one receptor: MC1R. The keyhole every Melanotan was cut to fit — and a melanoma risk gene.
